Document: Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents
Section: ## Stage 2
Part 3 of 3
==================================================
## Stage 2

## Medical Reports – all claims

## 7.1

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.1] (1) Save where paragraph (2) applies, the clamant should obtain a medical report, if one has not already been obtained.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.1] (2) In claims which consist of or include a whiplash injury, the claimant must obtain a medical report in accordance with paragraph 7.8C.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.1] 7.2 It is expected that most claimants will obtain a medical report from one expert, but additional medical reports may be obtained from other experts where the injuries require reports from more than one medical discipline.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.1] 7.3 The claimant must check the factual accuracy of any medical report before it is sent to the defendant.  There will be no further opportunity for the claimant to challenge the factual accuracy of a medical report after it has been sent to the defendant.

## 7.4

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (1) The medical expert should identify within the report—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (a) the medical records that have been reviewed; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (b) the medical records considered relevant to the claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (2) The claimant must disclose with any medical report sent to the defendant any medical records which the expert considers relevant.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] 7.5 In most claims with a value of no more than £10,000, it is expected that the medical expert will not need to see any medical records.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] 7.6 Any relevant photograph(s) of the claimant’s injuries upon which the claimant intends to rely should also be disclosed with the medical report.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] 7.7 Where the claimant was not wearing a seat belt the medical report must contain sufficient information to enable the defendant to calculate the appropriate reduction of damages in accordance with principles set out in existing case law.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] 7.8 A subsequent medical report from an expert who has already reported must be justified. A report may be justified where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (1) the first medical report recommends that further time is required before a prognosis of the claimant’s injuries can be determined; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (2) the claimant is receiving continuing treatment; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.4] (3) the claimant has not recovered as expected in the original prognosis.

## Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] 7.8A In addition to paragraphs 7.1 to 7.7, and subject to paragraph 7.8B, in a soft tissue injury claim—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] (1) the first report must be a fixed cost medical report from an accredited medical expert selected for the claim via the MedCo Portal (website at: www.medco.org.uk (opens in a new tab) ); and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] (2) where the defendant provides a different account under paragraph 6.19A, the claimant must provide this as part of the instructions to the medical expert for the sole purpose of asking the expert to comment on the impact, if any, on diagnosis and prognosis if—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] (a) the claimant’s account is found to be true; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Soft tissue injury claims – medical reports] (b) the defendant’s account is found to be true.

## 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (1) it is expected that only one medical report will be required;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (2) a further medical report, whether from the first expert instructed or from an expert in another discipline, will only be justified where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (a) it is recommended in the first expert’s report; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (b) that report has first been disclosed to the defendant; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (3) where the claimant obtains more than one medical report, the first report must be a fixed cost medical report from an accredited medical expert selected via the MedCo Portal and any further report from an expert in any of the following disciplines must also be a fixed cost medical report—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (a) Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (b) Consultant in Accident and Emergency Medicine;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (c) General Practitioner registered with the General Medical Council;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8B In a soft tissue injury claim—] (d) Physiotherapist registered with the Health and Care Professions Council.

## Claims which consist of, or include, a claim for whiplash injury – Medical Reports

## 7.8C

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (1) The provisions of paragraph 7.8A and 7.8B apply in respect of a medical report obtained under this paragraph, save that—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (a) any reference to soft tissue injury claim is to be read as referring to a claim which consists of, or includes, a claim for whiplash injury;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (b) paragraph (2) below applies in place of paragraph 7.8B(2).

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (2) A further report, whether from the first expert instructed or from an expert in another discipline, will only be justified where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (a) it is recommended in the first expert’s report;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (b) the first medical report recommends that further time is required before a prognosis of the claimant’s injuries can be determined;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (c) the claimant is receiving continuing treatment; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.8C] (d) the claimant has not recovered as expected in the original prognosis.

## Non-medical expert reports

## 7.9

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.9] (1) In most cases, a report from a non-medical expert will not be required, but a report may be obtained where it is reasonably required to value the claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.9] (2) Paragraph 7.3 applies to non-medical expert reports as it applies to expert medical reports.

## Specialist legal advice

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Specialist legal advice] 7.10 In most cases under this Protocol, it is expected that the claimant’s legal representative will be able to value the claim. In some cases with a value of more than £10,000 (excluding vehicle related damages), an additional advice from a specialist solicitor or from counsel may be justified where it is reasonably required to value the claim.

## Witness statements

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Witness statements] 7.11 In most cases, witness statements, whether from the claimant or otherwise, will not be, required.   One or more statements may, however, be provided where reasonably required to value the claim.

## Stay of process

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Stay of process] 7.12 Where the claimant needs to obtain a subsequent expert medical report or a non-medical report, the parties should agree to stay the process in this Protocol for a suitable period.  The claimant may then request an interim payment in accordance with paragraphs 7.13 to 7.16.

## Request for an interim payment

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Request for an interim payment] 7.13 Where the claimant requests an interim payment of £1,000, the defendant should make an interim payment to the claimant in accordance with paragraph 7.18.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Request for an interim payment] 7.14 The claimant must send to the defendant the Interim Settlement Pack and initial medical report(s) (including any recommendation that a subsequent medical report is justified) in order to request the interim payment.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Request for an interim payment] 7.14A In a claim which consists of or includes a claim for whiplash injury, the claimant must specify in the Interim Settlement pack how much of the interim payment request relates to—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Request for an interim payment] (a) the tariff amount; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Request for an interim payment] (b) the amount (if any) for damages in respect of any non-whiplash injuries.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Request for an interim payment] 7.15 The claimant must also send evidence of pecuniary losses and disbursements.  This will assist the defendant in considering whether to make an offer to settle the claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Request for an interim payment] 7.16 Where an interim payment of more than £1,000 is requested the claimant must specify in the Interim Settlement Pack the amount requested, the heads of damage which are the subject of the request and the reasons for the request.

## 7.17 Unless the parties agree otherwise or paragraph 7.17A applies—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.17 Unless the parties agree otherwise or paragraph 7.17A applies—] (a) the interim payment of £1,000 is only in relation to general damages; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.17 Unless the parties agree otherwise or paragraph 7.17A applies—] (b) where more than £1,000 is requested by the claimant, the amount in excess of £1,000 is only in relation to pecuniary losses.

## 7.17A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.17A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (a) the interim payment of £1,000 is to be applied first to the tariff amount;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.17A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (b) the balance of the £1,000 is to be applied first to general damages in respect of any non-whiplash injuries;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.17A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (c)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.17A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (i) any remaining balance of the £1,000; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.17A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (ii) where more than £1,000 is requested by the claimant, the amount in excess of £1,000,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.17A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] is only in relation to pecuniary losses.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.17A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (Paragraph 7.44B prohibits the parties from making or accepting any offer or payment in respect of a claim for whiplash injury until after the fixed cost medical report has been disclosed.)

## Interim payment of £1,000

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Interim payment of £1,000] 7.18 Where paragraph 7.13 applies the defendant must pay £1,000 within 10 days of receiving the Interim Settlement Pack.

## Interim payment of more than £1,000

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Interim payment of more than £1,000] 7.19 Subject to paragraphs 7.24 and 7.25, where the claimant has requested an interim payment of more than £1,000 the defendant must pay—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Interim payment of more than £1,000] (1) the full amount requested less any deductible amount which is payable to the CRU;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Interim payment of more than £1,000] (2) the amount of £1,000; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Interim payment of more than £1,000] (3) some other amount of more than £1,000 but less than the amount requested by the claimant, within 15 days of receiving the Interim Settlement Pack.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Interim payment of more than £1,000] 7.20 Where a payment is made under paragraphs 7.19(2) or (3) the defendant must briefly explain in the Interim Settlement Pack why the full amount requested by the claimant is not agreed.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Interim payment of more than £1,000] 7.21 Where the claim is valued at more than £10,000 the claimant may use the procedure at paragraphs 7.13 to 7.20 to request more than one interim payment.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Interim payment of more than £1,000] 7.22 Nothing in this Protocol is intended to affect the provisions contained in the Rehabilitation Code.

## Vehicle related damages – interim payments

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Vehicle related damages – interim payments] 7.23 Claims for vehicle related damages will ordinarily be dealt with outside the provisions of this Protocol under industry agreements between relevant organisations and insurers.  However, where the claimant has paid for the vehicle related damages, the sum may be included in a request for an interim payment under paragraph 7.16.

## Application for a certificate of recoverable benefits

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Application for a certificate of recoverable benefits] 7.24 Paragraph 7.25 applies where the defendant agrees to make a payment in accordance with paragraph 7.19(1) or (3) but does not yet have a certificate of recoverable benefits or does not have one that will remain in force for at least 10 days from the date of receiving the Interim Settlement Pack.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Application for a certificate of recoverable benefits] 7.25 The defendant should apply for a certificate of recoverable benefits as soon as possible, notify the claimant that it has done so and must make the interim payment under paragraph 7.19(1) or (3) no more than 30 days from the date of receiving the Interim Settlement Pack.

## Request for an interim payment where the claimant is a child

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Request for an interim payment where the claimant is a child] 7.26 The interim payment provisions in this Protocol do not apply where the claimant is a child.  Where the claimant is a child and an interim payment is reasonably required proceedings must be started under Part 7 of the CPR and an application for an interim payment can be made within those proceedings.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Request for an interim payment where the claimant is a child] (Rule 21.10 provides that no payment, which relates to a claim by a child, is valid without the approval of the court.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Request for an interim payment where the claimant is a child] 7.27 Paragraph 7.26 does not prevent a defendant from making a payment direct to a treatment provider.

## Interim payment – supplementary provisions

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Interim payment – supplementary provisions] 7.28 Where the defendant does not comply with paragraphs 7.18 or 7.19 the claimant may start proceedings under Part 7 of the CPR and apply to the court for an interim payment in those proceedings.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Interim payment – supplementary provisions] 7.29 Where the defendant does comply with paragraph 7.19(2) or (3) but the claimant is not content with the amount paid, the claimant may still start proceedings.  However, the court will order the defendant to pay no more than the Stage 2 fixed costs where the court awards an interim payment of no more than the amount offered by the defendant or the court makes no award.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Interim payment – supplementary provisions] 7.30 Where paragraph 7.28 or 7.29 applies the claimant must give notice to the defendant that the claim will no longer continue under this Protocol.  Unless the claimant’s notice is sent to the defendant within 10 days after the expiry of the period in paragraphs 7.18, 7.19 or 7.25 as appropriate, the claim will continue under this Protocol.

## Costs of expert medical and non-medical reports and specialist legal advice obtained

## 7.31

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.31] (1) Where the claimant obtains more than one expert report or an advice from a specialist solicitor or counsel—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.31] (a) the defendant at the end of Stage 2 may refuse to pay; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.31] (b) the court at Stage 3 may refuse to allow,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.31] the costs of any report or advice not reasonably required.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.31] (2) Therefore, where the claimant obtains more than one expert report or obtains an advice from a specialist solicitor or counsel—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.31] (a) the claimant should explain in the Stage 2 Settlement Pack  why they obtained a further report or such advice; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.31] (b) if relevant, the defendant should in the Stage 2 Settlement Pack    identify the report or reports or advice for which they will not pay and explain why they will not pay for that report or reports or advice.

## Submitting the Stage 2 Settlement Pack to the defendant

## 7.32 The Stage 2 Settlement Pack must comprise—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.32 The Stage 2 Settlement Pack must comprise—] (1) the Stage 2 Settlement Pack Form;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.32 The Stage 2 Settlement Pack must comprise—] (2) a medical report or reports;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.32 The Stage 2 Settlement Pack must comprise—] (3) evidence of pecuniary losses;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.32 The Stage 2 Settlement Pack must comprise—] (4) evidence of disbursements (for example the cost of any medical report);

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.32 The Stage 2 Settlement Pack must comprise—] (4A) in a soft tissue injury claim, the invoice for the cost of obtaining the fixed cost medical report and any invoice for the cost of obtaining medical records;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.32 The Stage 2 Settlement Pack must comprise—] (5) any non-medical expert report;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.32 The Stage 2 Settlement Pack must comprise—] (6) any medical records/photographs served with medical reports; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.32 The Stage 2 Settlement Pack must comprise—] (7) any witness statements.

## 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (1) the settlement pack must include the fixed cost medical report;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (2) the claimant’s offer in the settlement pack must set out separately—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (a) the tariff amount; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (b) the amount (if any) for damages in respect of any non-whiplash injuries;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (3) subject to paragraphs (4) and (5) below, the claimant may argue in accordance with the Whiplash Injury Regulations 2021 that there are exceptional circumstances which allow the claimant to seek an uplift on the tariff amount;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (4) a claimant who makes a request for an uplift under paragraph (3) must state in the settlement pack—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (a) the percentage uplift claimed up to a maximum of 20% and the amount claimed; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (b) how the whiplash injury is exceptionally severe; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (c) how the claimant’s circumstances increasing the pain, suffering or loss of amenity caused by their whiplash injury are exceptional.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] 7.32A In a soft tissue injury claim or a claim which consists of, or includes, a claim for whiplash injury, the Stage 2 Settlement Pack is of no effect unless the medical report is a fixed cost medical report. Where the claimant includes more than one medical report, the first report obtained must be a fixed cost medical report from an accredited medical expert selected via the MedCo Portal and any further report from an expert in any of the disciplines listed in paragraph 7.8B(3)(a) to (d) must also be a fixed cost medical report.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] 7.33 The claimant should send the Stage 2 Settlement Pack to the defendant within 15 days of the claimant approving —

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (1) the final medical report and agreeing to rely on the prognosis in that  report; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] (2) any non-medical expert report,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] whichever is later.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.A32A Where the claim consists of or includes a whiplash injury—] 7.34 Where the defendant alleges contributory negligence because of the claimant’s failure to wear a seat belt, the Stage 2 Settlement Pack Form must also suggest a percentage reduction (which may be 0 per cent) in the amount of damages.

## Consideration of claim

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Consideration of claim] 7.35 There is a 35 day period for consideration of the Stage 2 Settlement Pack by the defendant (“the total consideration period”).  This comprises a period of up to 15 days for the defendant to consider the Stage 2 Settlement Pack (“the initial consideration period”) and make an offer.  The remainder of the total consideration period (“the negotiation period”) is for any further negotiation between the parties.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Consideration of claim] 7.36 The total consideration period can be extended by the parties agreeing to extend either the initial consideration period or the negotiation period or both.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Consideration of claim] 7.37 Where a party makes an offer 5 days or less before the end of the total consideration period (including any extension to this period under paragraph 7.36), there will be a further period of 5 days after the end of the total consideration period for the relevant party to consider that offer.  During this period (“the further consideration period”) no further offers can be made by either party.

## Defendant accepts offer or makes counter-offer

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Defendant accepts offer or makes counter-offer] 7.38 Within the initial consideration period (or any extension agreed under paragraph 7.36) the defendant must either accept the offer made by the claimant on the Stage 2 Settlement Pack Form or make a counter-offer using that form.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Defendant accepts offer or makes counter-offer] 7.39 The claim will no longer continue under this Protocol where the defendant gives notice to the claimant within the initial consideration period (or any extension agreed under paragraph 7.36) that the defendant—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Defendant accepts offer or makes counter-offer] (a) considers that, if proceedings were started, the small claims track would be the normal track for that claim; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Defendant accepts offer or makes counter-offer] (b) withdraws the admission of causation as defined in paragraph

## 1.1(1)(c).

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] 7.40 Where the defendant does not respond within the initial consideration period (or any extension agreed under paragraph 7.36), the claim will no longer continue under this Protocol and the claimant may start proceedings under Part 7 of the CPR.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] 7.41 When making a counter-offer the defendant must propose an amount for each head of damage and may, in addition, make an offer that is higher than the total of the amounts proposed for all heads of damage. The defendant must also explain in the counter-offer why a particular head of damage has been reduced.  The explanation will assist the claimant when negotiating a settlement and will allow both parties to focus on those areas of the claim that remain in dispute.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] 7.41A Where the claim consists of or includes a claim for whiplash injury, the defendant’s counter-offer in the settlement pack must set out separately—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] (a) the tariff amount;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] (b) the amount (if any) for damages in respect of any non-whiplash injuries; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] (c) where the claimant has requested an uplift, the percentage and amount (if any) for the uplift.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] 7.42 Where the defendant has obtained a certificate of recoverable benefits from the CRU the counter-offer must state the name and amount of any deductible amount.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] 7.43 On receipt of a counter-offer from the defendant the claimant has until the end of the total consideration period or the further consideration period to accept or decline the counter offer.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] 7.44 Any offer to settle made at any stage by either party will automatically include, and cannot exclude—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] (1) the Stage 1 and Stage 2 fixed costs in Table 10 in Practice Direction 45;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] (2) an agreement in principle to pay a sum equal to the Type C fixed costs of an additional advice on quantum of damages where such advice is justified under paragraph 7.10;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] (3) an agreement in principle to pay relevant disbursements allowed in accordance with rule 45.58;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] (3A) in a soft tissue injury claim, the cost of obtaining a medical report in rule 45.62(2)(a); or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] (3B) in a claim which consists of or includes a claim for whiplash injury, the cost of obtaining the fixed cost medical report in paragraph 1.14 of Practice Direction 27B.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1(1)(c).] 7.44A In a soft tissue injury claim, an offer to settle made by either party before a fixed cost medical report has been obtained and disclosed will have no adverse costs consequences until after the report has been disclosed.

## 7.44B In a claim that consists of or includes a claim for whiplash injury—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.44B In a claim that consists of or includes a claim for whiplash injury—] (a) no offer may be made, invited or accepted by either party, and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.44B In a claim that consists of or includes a claim for whiplash injury—] (b) no payment may be made by the defendant or accepted by the claimant,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.44B In a claim that consists of or includes a claim for whiplash injury—] in respect of the claim for whiplash injury until after the fixed cost medical report has been disclosed.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.44B In a claim that consists of or includes a claim for whiplash injury—] 7.45 Where there is a dispute about whether an additional advice on quantum of damages is justified or about the amount or validity of any disbursement, the parties may use the procedure set out in rule 45.40.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 7.44B In a claim that consists of or includes a claim for whiplash injury—] (Rule 45.40 provides that where the parties to a dispute have a written agreement on all issues but have failed to agree the amount of the costs, they may start proceedings under that rule so that the court can determine the amount of those costs.)

## Withdrawal of offer after the consideration period

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Withdrawal of offer after the consideration period] 7.46 Where a party withdraws an offer made in the Stage 2 Settlement Pack Form after the total consideration period or further consideration period, the claim will no longer continue under this Protocol and the claimant may start proceedings under Part 7 of the CPR.

## Settlement

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] 7.47 Except where the claimant is a child or paragraphs 7.49 and 7.50 apply, the defendant must pay—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (1) the agreed damages less any—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (a) deductible amount which is payable to the CRU; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (b) previous interim payment;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (2) any unpaid Stage 1 fixed costs in Table 10 in Practice Direction 45;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (3) the Stage 2 fixed costs in Table 10 in Practice Direction 45;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (4) where an additional advice on quantum of damages is justified under paragraph 7.10, a sum equal to the Type C fixed costs to cover the cost of that advice;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (5) the relevant disbursements allowed in accordance with rule 45.58 including any disbursements fixed under rule 45.62(2); and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (6) where applicable, any success fee in accordance with rule 45.31(1) (as it was in force immediately before 1 April 2013),

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] within 10 days of the parties agreeing a settlement.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (Rule 21.10 provides that the approval of the court is required where, before proceedings are started, a claim is made by a child and a settlement is reached.  The provisions in paragraph 6.1 of Practice Direction 49F set out what must be filed with the court when an application is made to approve a settlement.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] 7.48 Except where paragraph 7.51 applies, where the parties agree a settlement for a greater sum than the defendant had offered during the total consideration period or further consideration period and after the Court Proceedings Pack has been sent to the defendant but before proceedings are issued under Stage 3—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Settlement] (1) paragraph 7.47 applies; and
